issues.claim: Running costs include "Web chat agent messages: $6.24/month at 300 AI messages" ($0.0208 per AI message, Retell chat agent pricing).
issues.problem: No chat channel exists anywhere in the solution design, components, integrations, phases or pilot scope - the web front door is a self-built Next.js guided intake, not a Retell chat agent. The unit price is correct, but this line prices a component that is not being built, which inflates the stated total by $6.24 and makes the $275 fee reasoning slightly conservative in the wrong place.
issues.fix: Either add a Retell web-chat channel to the design/components, or drop the line and restate the total as $55.55/month (22.35 + 2.00 + 24.00 + 6.00 + 1.20).

issues.claim: Retell pricing basis accounts for the full cost of the voice channel at $0.149/minute (voice infra + platform voices + LLM + telephony).
issues.problem: Retell's docs state that after a warm transfer connects, the agent fee stops but telephony charges continue until the transferred call ends; the plan's per-minute basis and 150-minute volume do not mention these post-handoff telephony minutes, which the design will generate every time the agent warm-transfers to a partner.
issues.fix: Add a sentence to the voice-cost line that post-transfer telephony minutes are billed at $0.015/min on top of the 150 agent minutes, and note the tail is small but non-zero.

issues.claim: "Estimated total running cost at pilot volumes: $61.79/month" is cited to https://www.retellai.com/pricing.
issues.problem: The arithmetic is right ($22.35 + $2.00 + $6.24 + $24.00 + $6.00 + $1.20 = $61.79), but the line's single source URL is Retell's page while the sum also includes Cal.com, DigitalOcean, DigitalOcean backups and Resend items priced from four other pages.
issues.fix: Point the total line at a cost table summary (or list the underlying source URLs) rather than at Retell pricing alone.

issues.claim: Pilot schedule: "weeks 1-4 are build ... 13.5 of the 17.5 founder-days" at "about 3 founder-days a week".
issues.problem: 13.5 days across four weeks at 3 days/week is 12 days; the plan's own rate implies the build needs about 4.5 weeks. Day totals themselves are consistent (2+5+2+1.5+3+1 = 17.5; 17.5/3 = 5.83 weeks), so the mismatch is only in the week-by-week split.
issues.fix: Say build may spill into week 5 before web intake goes live, or state the build rate as 3.5 days/week.

issues.claim: Suggested pricing and feasibility reasoning lean on "the audit's own impact estimate of $2,500-$9,287/year in recovered staff time".
issues.problem: That figure comes from an internal artifact (audit.md) that is not in this verification folder and is not a public source, so it could not be re-checked here. It is at least labeled as the audit's estimate rather than as published data.
issues.fix: Carry the audit figure with an explicit "internal estimate, not independently sourced" label, or restate the fee argument from the verified cost base and competitor prices alone.

issues.claim: Retell knowledge base line notes "$8.00 per knowledge base per month" and "the first 10 knowledge bases are free".
issues.problem: Both statements do appear on Retell's pricing page (the page is internally inconsistent, showing both a per-KB price and a free allowance of 10), so the plan is faithful to the source, but the $0 line rests on the free allowance rather than on the published $8 price.
issues.fix: No change required to the number; if a knowledge base is ever used, re-check which statement applies before quoting $0.

NJ AI guidelines quote RPC 1.6(f) language on preventing inadvertent or unauthorized disclosure and state a lawyer is responsible to ensure the security of an AI system before entering non-public client information.
NJ AI guidelines extend oversight to the ethical use of AI by other lawyers and nonlawyer staff, citing RPC 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3.

NJ AI guidelines say AI will affect billing and advertising, citing RPC 1.5 and 7.2, and that no per-use AI disclosure duty exists but disclosure is required if the client asks or cannot make an informed decision.
The Jan 24, 2024 AI guidelines do not cite RPC 7.1 (so the 7.1 point must be cited to the rule text, as the plan does).
N.J.S.A. 2A:156A-4(d) permits interception where the person is a party or one party has given prior consent, unless used for a criminal/tortious or other injurious act.

47 CFR 64.1200(a)(1) bars artificial/prerecorded-voice calls without prior express consent except emergency calls; (b)(1) requires stating the business identity at the start of the message; (a)(10) treats stop/quit/end/revoke/opt out/cancel/unsubscribe replies as per-se revocation with honouring within ten business days.
RPC 5.5(a)(2) bars assisting a nonlawyer in activity constituting the unauthorized practice of law.
RPC 5.4(a) bars sharing legal fees with a nonlawyer except listed exceptions; RPC 5.4(c) bars a nonlawyer who recommends/employs/pays the lawyer from directing professional judgment.
RPC 7.1(a)(2) prohibits communications likely to create an unjustified expectation about results; 7.1(a)(3) covers comparisons lacking the name, substantiation and disclaimer.
RPC 5.3 requires reasonable efforts to ensure a nonlawyer's conduct is compatible with the lawyer's professional obligations.
The official njcourts.gov RPC PDF (sites/default/files/rpc.pdf) returns a not-found page, which is why the plan cites a third-party compilation.
Firm contact page lists phone hours "Mon-Fri from 9AM to 5PM" with no after-hours or emergency line.
The site says a consultation is scheduled "by calling our office or filling out the contact form", with no self-scheduling widget.
The Webflow form is native, redirects to /thank-you and carries a Cloudflare Turnstile site key.
Google Tag Manager GTM-ML8VXZ7C and GA4 G-8WYZ2PDNST are installed site-wide.
Partner emails Pankaj@wileylavender.com and larry@wileylavender.com are published on the site.
The firm self-reports "200+ successful cases per year" and has seven practice areas matching the intake taxonomy.
The site carries inconsistent client counts (1K+ on /services, 5K+ on /our-history) as the risk section notes.
